campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution authorizing an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority to accept low-carbon transportation program funding for a transit reliability and performance improvement project. The agenda also referenced pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a low-carbon transportation and operations program fund agreement with VTA for a transit reliability and performance systems project
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine items like meeting minutes, vendor payments, and the monthly Treasurer's Report, and considered responses to two Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims processing and VTA's oversight of the BART Silicon Valley Phase II project. The Council also considered a state bill on utility data transparency, a contract for a transportation impact fee study, forming a committee on alternative policing services, and discussed the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and the city's involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a state bill on utility billing data transparency
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
The future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued participation in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine business including updated pay schedules for city employee groups, a $250,000 increase to an electrical maintenance contract, and reorganizing the volunteer awards committee to be Los Altos-only. Council also considered renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, discussed a citizen initiative on zoning impacts, and set up a subcommittee for the City Manager's annual performance review.
keyTopics: Resolution to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street
Revised FY 2026/27 pay schedules for employee associations and unrepresented staff
$250,000 increase to the Bear Electrical Solutions maintenance agreement
Disbanding the joint Los Altos–Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee in favor of a Los Altos-only committee
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes from several August sessions and took up a handful of other items, including vacating a public service easement at a Cerro Vista address, setting up preferential and time-limited parking in a certain area, and authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-level work.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-related services
Approval of minutes from multiple August 2026 Town Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 2, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to plan upcoming City Council schedules, canceling the September 8, 2026 meeting and reviewing the draft agenda for September 15, 2026. The committee also considered the City Clerk's public record log for late August and took up a study session on financing tools that could support economic development infrastructure projects.
keyTopics: Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 Council meeting
Review and possible additions to the September 15, 2026 draft agenda
Public record log covering August 20–27, 2026
Study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee — September 10, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee held a meeting where city staff were on hand to answer questions from residents about neighborhood issues. Community members had the option to submit their questions ahead of time online.
keyTopics: City staff Q&A session on neighborhood-related questions

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: Sunnyvale's City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, starting with a closed session for confidential discussion, followed by a public session that included a presentation on updates to the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — September 9, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission kicked off its new term by swearing in incoming commissioners for 2026-2028 and holding an orientation session. The Commission also received a presentation on teen programs and considered approval of minutes from its August 12, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Swearing-in ceremony for incoming 2026-2028 Teen Commissioners
Teen Commission orientation for new members
Presentation on teen programs
Approval of August 12, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, with one councilmember (Chahal) participating remotely from India. Based on the available agenda information, no specific policy items or discussion topics were detailed beyond the remote participation logistics and public comment procedures.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format with in-person and Zoom remote access options for the public

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: This meeting of the Successor Agency to the former Redevelopment Agency addressed housekeeping and financial matters tied to winding down redevelopment debt. The Council, sitting as the Successor Agency Board, considered confirming which city officials hold official roles for the Agency and considered authorizing the sale of refunding bonds to replace older redevelopment-era debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance existing redevelopment debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — September 4, 2026
palo-alto.summary: Palo Alto's Climate Action and Sustainability Committee reviewed an early look at the city's 2025 greenhouse gas inventory, including a discussion of Scope 3 emissions (indirect emissions from things like supply chains and purchased goods). The committee also considered different approaches the city could take to reach its carbon neutrality goal and gave feedback on what areas staff should study further.
keyTopics: Preliminary review of the 2025 greenhouse gas inventory
Overview of Scope 3 emissions
Approaches to achieving the city's carbon neutrality goal
Committee feedback on areas for further staff analysis
